newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close higher before All Saints.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close higher before All Saints.

text.p: French shares closed higher on Thursday before the All Saints holiday with only the expiry of the October options contract in the late afternoon giving a sparkle to otherwise listless trading.

The market did not react to a record September unemployment rate of 12.6 percent and shrugged off a five basis point rate cut by the Bank of France. It took hardly notice of September U.S. jobless claims and consumer spending. But after Wall Street opened and towards the 1500 GMT expiry things livened up.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 15.75 points or 0.74 percent at 2,140.51. Volume was 7.25 billion francs.
Of the volume, six billion francs was related to so-called basket deals prompted by the expiry of the October future contract.
The October future closed at 2,142 on Thursday, against a Wednesday settlement at 2,128.50.
Despite the higher close on Thursday, the blue-chip index was down 1.01 percent on the week due to profit-taking after hitting a two-and-a-half year high last week.
The franc was supported by a European Commission decision to allow France to use a special France Telecom payment towards cutting the budget deficit and single currency qualification.
* Lagardere posted 3.8 percent gain to 161.50 francs as some recent Thomson bid worries subsided.
* Euro Disney made a 4.74 percent loss ahead of its financial year results on November 14.
* LVMH gained a further 1.56 percent to 1,171 francs on the back of Wednesday's announcement it planned to buy a majority stake in DFS of the U.S. for 12.6 billion francs.
* Roussel-Uclaf jumped 1.88 percent to 1,353 francs on reports Hoescht may buy out minorities at 1,600. Roussel-Uclaf finance director Daniel Camus told Reuters no decision had been taken.
* Car stocks Peugeot down 0.37 percent at 533 and Renault up 0.09 percent at 110.30 francs.
Industry sources said the October car registrations, to be published on Monday, were up 25 percent, despite expiry of a buy premium scheme, compared with a relatively low October in 1995.
* Alcatel Alsthom, up 0.51 pct at 436 francs, sold its 2.2 percent stake in Lafarge LAFA.PA, up 1.25 percent to 306.80 francs, to the company for 660 million francs.
* Suez chief executive Gerard Mestrallet told a Belgian newspaper it was likely to sell Generale de Belgique's nine percent stake in Accor, up 1.26 percent at 642.

* Thomson-CSF closed unchanged at 159.50. On Wednesday, after the Bourse closed, the company reported a higher first half net attributable profit and said it expected to post a profit for 1996 after three years of losses.
